- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- After sharp price spikes, model frequently overshoots in the next few days; apply a downward correction of 1–3% for the immediate following period.
- If model shows strong upward trend but sentiment is weak or negative, reduce slope or add drag to prevent overcorrection.
- Mean reversion is evident when model forecasts diverge >5% from recent 7-day average; bring forecast closer to moving average.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently higher than model, especially after sentiment shifts to positive, model may be under-reacting — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% per sentiment shift.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and model is flat, consider slight upward bias — prices often rise modestly in such regimes.
